048/**
049 * Data Type Conversion Tables;
050 * Appendix B of JDBC 4.2 Specification JSR 221, March 2014.
051 * In this class the tables are usually {@link ImmutableListMultimap}s,
052 * jdbcTypeToClass is an exception, it's based on an EnumMap.
053 * In addition to the tables, there is a method with the same name as the
054 * table which takes a key as a parameter
055 * and generally returns the first item in the list;
056 * see {@link #jdbcTypeToClassStrict(java.sql.JDBCType) } for an exception.
057 * <p>
058 * Table B.3 is updated for the {@code java1.8} and later world.
059 */
060public class JdbcDataTypeConversionTables {
061  private JdbcDataTypeConversionTables() {}
062
063  /**
064   * Map JdbcType to Java Object Class;  JDBC 4.2 spec, Appendix B Table 3.
065   * <p>
066   * The differences from spec with their return values are
067   * <ul>
068   * <li> TINYINT Byte
069   * <li> SMALLINT Short
070   * <li> DATE java.time.LocalDate
071   * <li> TIME java.time.LocalTime
072   * <li> TIMESTAMP java.time.LocalDateTime
073   * <li> TIME_WITH_TIMEZONE java.time.OffetTime
074   * <li> TIMESTAMP_WITH_TIMEZONE java.time.OffetDateTime
075   * </ul>
076   * <p>
077   * Note that {@code TIME_WITH_TIMEZONE}
078   * and {@code TIMESTAMP_WITH_TIMEZONE }
079   * are not found at all in Table 3.
080   * <p>
081   * Use {@link #jdbcTypeToClassStrict(java.sql.JDBCType) } for strict
082   * adherence to the spec.
083   *
084   * @param type JDBCType
085   * @return corresponding java object class
086   */
087  public static Class<?> jdbcTypeToClass(JDBCType type) {
088    List<Class<?>> l = (List<Class<?>>) jdbcTypeToClass.get(type);
089    return l == null || l.isEmpty() ? null : l.get(0);
090  }
091
092  @SuppressWarnings("unused")
093  private static final Set<JDBCType> hasStrictJavaTypeClass
094      = EnumSet.of(TINYINT, SMALLINT, DATE, TIME, TIMESTAMP);
095
096  @SuppressWarnings("unused")
097  private static final Set<JDBCType> tzStrictJavaTypeClass
098      = EnumSet.of(TIME_WITH_TIMEZONE, TIMESTAMP_WITH_TIMEZONE);
099
100  /**
101   * Map JdbcType to Java Object Class;  JDBC 4.2 spec, Appendix B Table 3.
102   *
103   * @param type JDBCType
104   * @return corresponding java object class
105   */
106  public static Class<?> jdbcTypeToClassStrict(JDBCType type) {
107    List<Class<?>> l = (List<Class<?>>) jdbcTypeToClass.get(type);
108
109    // TODO: Use EnumSets to decide?
110
111    return switch (type) {
112      case TINYINT, SMALLINT, DATE, TIME, TIMESTAMP -> l.get(1);
113      case TIME_WITH_TIMEZONE, TIMESTAMP_WITH_TIMEZONE -> null;
114      default -> l == null || l.isEmpty() ? null : l.get(0);
115    };
116  }
117
118  /**
119   * Map Java Object to JdbcTypes; JDBC 4.2 spec, Appendix B Table 4
120   * <p>
121   * Note that the elements of the map are a list;
122   * typically do {@code ClassToJDBCType.get(String.class).get(0)}
123   * to get an item.
124   * @param _clazz class to lookup
125   * @return jdbc type corresponding to class
126   */
127  public static JDBCType classToJdbcType(Class<?> _clazz) {
128    ImmutableList<JDBCType> l = classToJdbcType.get(_clazz);
129    return l.isEmpty() ? null : l.get(0);
130  }
131
132  /**
133   * Map JdbcType to Java Object;  JDBC 4.2 spec, Appendix B Table 3.
134   * <p>
135   * <b>Implementation note:</b>
136   * <p>
137   * The JDBC 4.2 spec only has one class listed per JDBCType since they
138   * are the types returned by getObject for a given type. However, for
139   * certain types (not constrained to JDBC 1.0) newer JDK types are
140   * recommended and of course there are the new *WITH_TIMEZONE types.
141   * Since this is a list multimap, the updated information is included
142   * and is provided by the default method
143   * {@link #jdbcTypeToClass(java.sql.JDBCType) }; see that method's javadoc
144   * for the details of the change.
145   * To get strict adherence to the spec,
146   * use {@link #jdbcTypeToClassStrict(java.sql.JDBCType) }
147   */
148  public static final Map<JDBCType, Collection<Class<?>>> jdbcTypeToClass = createTable3();
149
150  // Want immutable EnumListMultimap, but it doesn't exist
151  // https://github.com/google/guava/issues/977
152
153  /**
154   * Guava has no immutable enum multimap, so...
155   * @return unmodifiable enum multimap
156   */
157  private static Map<JDBCType, Collection<Class<?>>> createTable3() {
158    ListMultimap<JDBCType, Class<?>> table3
159        = MultimapBuilder.enumKeys(JDBCType.class).arrayListValues(2).build();
160    table3.put(CHAR, String.class);
161    table3.put(VARCHAR, String.class);
162    table3.put(LONGVARCHAR, String.class);
163    table3.put(NUMERIC, java.math.BigDecimal.class);
164    table3.put(DECIMAL, java.math.BigDecimal.class);
165    table3.put(BIT, Boolean.class);
166    table3.put(BOOLEAN, Boolean.class);
167
168    table3.putAll(TINYINT, List.of(Byte.class, Integer.class));
169    table3.putAll(SMALLINT, List.of(Short.class, Integer.class));
170
171    table3.put(INTEGER, Integer.class);
172    table3.put(BIGINT, Long.class);
173    table3.put(REAL, Float.class);
174    table3.put(FLOAT, Double.class);
175    table3.put(DOUBLE, Double.class);
176    table3.put(BINARY, byte[].class);
177    table3.put(VARBINARY, byte[].class);
178    table3.put(LONGVARBINARY, byte[].class);
179
180    table3.putAll(DATE, List.of(java.time.LocalDate.class, java.sql.Date.class));
181    table3.putAll(TIME, List.of(java.time.LocalTime.class, java.sql.Time.class));
182    table3.putAll(TIMESTAMP, List.of(java.time.LocalDateTime.class, java.sql.Timestamp.class));
183
184    table3.put(TIME_WITH_TIMEZONE, java.time.OffsetTime.class);
185    table3.put(TIMESTAMP_WITH_TIMEZONE, java.time.OffsetDateTime.class);
186    // DISTINCTObject type of underlying type.class);
187    table3.put(CLOB, java.sql.Clob.class);
188    table3.put(BLOB, java.sql.Blob.class);
189    table3.put(ARRAY, java.sql.Array.class);
190    // STRUCT java.sql.Struct or.class or java.sql.SQLData.class;
191    table3.put(REF, java.sql.Ref.class);
192    table3.put(DATALINK, java.net.URL.class);
193    // JAVA_OBJECT Underlying Java class.class;
194    table3.put(ROWID, java.sql.RowId.class);
195    table3.put(NCHAR, String.class);
196    table3.put(NVARCHAR, String.class);
197    table3.put(LONGNVARCHAR, String.class);
198    table3.put(NCLOB, java.sql.NClob.class);
199    table3.put(SQLXML, java.sql.SQLXML.class);
200
201    return Multimaps.unmodifiableListMultimap(table3).asMap();
202  }
203
204  /**
205   * Map Java Object to JdbcTypes; JDBC 4.2 spec, Appendix B Table 4
206   * <p>
207   * Note that the elements of the map are a list.
208   * Typically use the method {@link #classToJdbcType(java.lang.Class) }
209   * which returns the first JDBCType for the class with
210   * {@code ClassToJDBCType.get(Some.class).get(0)}
211   * to get an item.
212   */
213  public static final ImmutableListMultimap<Class<?>, JDBCType> classToJdbcType
214      = ImmutableListMultimap.<Class<?>, JDBCType>builder()
215            .putAll(String.class, CHAR, VARCHAR, LONGVARCHAR, NCHAR, NVARCHAR, LONGNVARCHAR)
216            // include DECIMAL
217            .put(java.math.BigDecimal.class, NUMERIC)
218            .putAll(Boolean.class, BIT, BOOLEAN)
219            // note Byte not Integer
220            .put(Byte.class, TINYINT)
221            // note Short not Integer
222            .put(Short.class, SMALLINT)
223            .put(Integer.class, INTEGER)
224            .put(Long.class, BIGINT)
225            .put(Float.class, REAL)
226            // include FLOAT
227            .putAll(Double.class, DOUBLE, FLOAT)
228            .putAll(byte[].class, BINARY, VARBINARY, LONGVARBINARY)
229            .put(java.math.BigInteger.class, BIGINT)
230            .put(java.sql.Date.class, DATE)
231            .put(java.sql.Time.class, TIME)
232            .put(java.sql.Timestamp.class, TIMESTAMP)
233            .put(java.sql.Clob.class, CLOB)
234            .put(java.sql.Blob.class, BLOB)
235            .put(java.sql.Array.class, ARRAY)
236            .put(java.sql.Struct.class, STRUCT)
237            .put(java.sql.Ref.class, REF)
238            .put(java.net.URL.class, DATALINK)
239
240            .put(Object.class, JAVA_OBJECT)
241
242            .put(java.sql.RowId.class, ROWID)
243            .put(java.sql.NClob.class, NCLOB)
244            .put(java.sql.SQLXML.class, SQLXML)
245            .put(java.util.Calendar.class, TIMESTAMP)
246            .put(java.util.Date.class, TIMESTAMP)
247            .put(java.time.LocalDate.class, DATE)
248            .put(java.time.LocalTime.class, TIME)
249            .put(java.time.LocalDateTime.class, TIMESTAMP)
250            .put(java.time.OffsetTime.class, TIME_WITH_TIMEZONE)
251            .put(java.time.OffsetDateTime.class, TIMESTAMP_WITH_TIMEZONE)
252            .build();
253
254  private static Map<String, JDBCType> arrayTypeMap;
255  /**
256   * Map of vendor-specific primitive typenames to standard JDBCType.
257   * Thanks to Google AI.
258   * The AI claims this works with PostgreSQL, H2, HSQLDB, ClickHouse, MySQL/TiDB,
259   * Oracle, DuckDB, and SQL Server.
260   * See {@link dev.visdb.seesaw.datasources.DbSupport#resolveArrayElementType(java.sql.ResultSetMetaData, int) resolveArrayElementType(ResultSetMetaData, int)}
261   * @return
262   */
263  public static Map<String, JDBCType> vendorTypeMap() {
264    // clang-format off
265    if (arrayTypeMap == null ) {
266      arrayTypeMap = Map.ofEntries(
267        entry("INT", JDBCType.INTEGER),
268        entry("INT4", JDBCType.INTEGER),
269        entry("INT32", JDBCType.INTEGER),
270        entry("INTEGER", JDBCType.INTEGER),
271        entry("MEDIUMINT", JDBCType.INTEGER),
272        entry("BIGINT", JDBCType.BIGINT),
273        entry("INT8", JDBCType.BIGINT),
274        entry("INT64", JDBCType.BIGINT),
275        entry("SMALLINT", JDBCType.SMALLINT),
276        entry("INT2", JDBCType.SMALLINT),
277        entry("TINYINT", JDBCType.TINYINT),
278        entry("INT1", JDBCType.TINYINT),
279
280        // String / Character variants
281        entry("VARCHAR", JDBCType.VARCHAR),
282        entry("VARCHAR2", JDBCType.VARCHAR),
283        entry("TEXT", JDBCType.VARCHAR),
284        entry("CHAR", JDBCType.CHAR),
285        entry("BPCHAR", JDBCType.CHAR), // PostgreSQL Blank Padded Char
286        entry("NVARCHAR", JDBCType.NVARCHAR),
287
288        // Floating point numbers
289        entry("FLOAT", JDBCType.FLOAT),
290        entry("FLOAT4", JDBCType.REAL),
291        entry("REAL", JDBCType.REAL),
292        entry("DOUBLE", JDBCType.DOUBLE),
293        entry("DOUBLE PRECISION", JDBCType.DOUBLE),
294        entry("FLOAT8", JDBCType.DOUBLE),
295
296        // Numeric / Exact Decimals
297        entry("NUMERIC", JDBCType.NUMERIC),
298        entry("DECIMAL", JDBCType.DECIMAL),
299
300        // Boolean variants
301        entry("BOOL", JDBCType.BOOLEAN),
302        entry("BOOLEAN", JDBCType.BOOLEAN),
303
304        // Date and Time
305        entry("DATE", JDBCType.DATE),
306        entry("TIME", JDBCType.TIME),
307        entry("TIMESTAMP", JDBCType.TIMESTAMP),
308        entry("TIMESTAMPTZ", JDBCType.TIMESTAMP_WITH_TIMEZONE),
309
310        // Binary fields
311        entry("BYTEA", JDBCType.VARBINARY),
312        entry("BLOB", JDBCType.BLOB)
313      );
314    }
315    // clang-format on
316    return arrayTypeMap;
317  }

321  // Below here are copied from the spec.
322
323  // B.1 JDBC Types Mapped to Java Types
324  // ===================================
325  // TABLE B-1 shows the conceptual correspondence between JDBC types and Java types.
326  // A programmer should write code with this mapping in mind. For example, if a
327  // value in the database is a SMALLINT, a short should be the data type used in a
328  // JDBC application.
329  // All CallableStatement getter methods except for getObject use this mapping.
330  // The getObject methods for both the CallableStatement and ResultSet
331  // interfaces use the mapping in TABLE B-3.
332  // TABLE B-1 JDBC Types Mapped to Java Types
333  // -----------------------------------
334
335  /*
336  JdbcAppxB_1
337
338  CHAR String
339  VARCHAR String
340  LONGVARCHAR String
341  NUMERIC java.math.BigDecimal
342  DECIMAL java.math.BigDecimal
343  BIT boolean
344  BOOLEAN boolean
345  TINYINT byte
346  SMALLINT short
347  INTEGER int
348  BIGINT long
349  REAL float
350  FLOAT double
351  DOUBLE double
352  BINARY byte[]
353  VARBINARY byte[]
354  LONGVARBINARY byte[]
355  DATE java.sql.Date
356  TIME java.sql.Time
357  TIMESTAMP java.sql.Timestamp
358  CLOB java.sql.Clob
359  BLOB java.sql.Blob
360  ARRAY java.sql.array
361  DISTINCT Mapping of underlying type
362  STRUCT java.sql.Struct
363  REF java.sql.Ref
364  DATALINK java.net.URL
365  JAVA_OBJECT Underlying Java class
366  ROWID java.sql.RowId
367  NCHAR String
368  NVARCHAR String
369  LONGNVARCHAR String
370  NCLOB java.sql.NClob
371  SQLXML java.sql.SQLXML
372  */
373
374  // B.2 Java Types Mapped to JDBC Types
375  // ===================================
376  // TABLE B-2 shows the mapping a driver should use for the updater methods in the
377  // ResultSet interface and for IN parameters. PreparedStatement setter methods
378  // and RowSet setter methods use this table for mapping an IN parameter, which is a
379  // Java type, to the JDBC type that will be sent to the database. Note that the
380  // setObject methods for these two interfaces use the mapping shown in TABLE B-4.
381  // TABLE B-2 Standard Mapping from Java Types to JDBC Types
382  // -----------------------------------
383
384  /*
385  JdbcAppxB_2
386
387  String CHAR, VARCHAR, LONGVARCHAR, NCHAR,
388          NVARCHAR, LONGNVARCHAR
389  java.math.BigDecimal NUMERIC
390  boolean BIT, BOOLEAN
391  byte TINYINT
392  short SMALLINT
393  int INTEGER
394  long BIGINT
395  float REAL
396  double DOUBLE
397  byte[] BINARY, VARBINARY, LONGVARBINARY
398  java.sql.Date DATE
399  java.sql.Time TIME
400  java.sql.Timestamp TIMESTAMP
401  java.sql.Clob CLOB
402  java.sql.Blob BLOB
403  java.sql.Array ARRAY
404  java.sql.Struct STRUCT
405  java.sql.Ref REF
406  java.net.URL DATALINK
407  Java class JAVA_OBJECT
408  java.sql.RowId ROWID
409  java.sql.NClob NCLOB
410  java.sql.SQLXML SQLXML
411  */
412
413  // B.3 JDBC Types Mapped to Java Object Types
414  // ===================================
415  // ResultSet.getObject and CallableStatement.getObject use the mapping
416  // shown in TABLE B-3 for standard mappings.
417  // Note – The JDBC 1.0 specification defined the Java object mapping for the
418  // SMALLINT and TINYINT JDBC types to be Integer. The Java language did not
419  // include the Byte and Short data types when the JDBC 1.0 specification was
420  // finalized. The mapping of SMALLINT and TINYINT to Integer is maintained to
421  // preserve backwards compatibility.
422  // TABLE B-3 Mapping from JDBC Types to Java Object Types
423  // -----------------------------------
424
425  /*
426  JdbcAppxB_3
427
428  CHAR String
429  VARCHAR String
430  LONGVARCHAR String
431  NUMERIC java.math.BigDecimal
432  DECIMAL java.math.BigDecimal
433  BIT Boolean
434  BOOLEAN Boolean
435  TINYINT Integer
436  SMALLINT Integer
437  INTEGER Integer
438  BIGINT Long
439  REAL Float
440  FLOAT Double
441  DOUBLE Double
442  BINARY byte[]
443  VARBINARY byte[]
444  LONGVARBINARY byte[]
445  DATE java.sql.Date
446  TIME java.sql.Time
447  TIMESTAMP java.sql.Timestamp
448  DISTINCT Object type of underlying type
449  CLOB java.sql.Clob
450  BLOB java.sql.Blob
451  ARRAY java.sql.Array
452  STRUCT java.sql.Struct or
453  java.sql.SQLData
454  REF java.sql.Ref
455  DATALINK java.net.URL
456  JAVA_OBJECT Underlying Java class
457  ROWID java.sql.RowId
458  NCHAR String
459  NVARCHAR String
460  LONGNVARCHAR String
461  NCLOB java.sql.NClob
462  SQLXML java.sql.SQLXML
463  */
464

481  Short SMALLINT

484  Float REAL
485  Double DOUBLE
486  byte[] BINARY, VARBINARY, LONGVARBINARY
487  java.math.BigInteger BIGINT
488  java.sql.Date DATE
489  java.sql.Time TIME
490  java.sql.Timestamp TIMESTAMP
491  java.sql.Clob CLOB
492  java.sql.Blob BLOB
493  java.sql.Array ARRAY
494  java.sql.Struct STRUCT
495  java.sql.Ref REF
496  java.net.URL DATALINK
497  Java class JAVA_OBJECT
498  java.sql.RowId ROWID
499  java.sql.NClob NCLOB

508  */

576  // B.6 Type Conversions Supported by ResultSet getter Methods
577  // ===================================
578  // TABLE B-6 shows which JDBC types may be returned by ResultSet getter methods.
579  // This table also shows the conversions used by the SQLInput reader methods, except
580  // that they use only the recommended conversions.
581  // TABLE B-6 Use of ResultSet getter Methods to Retrieve JDBC Data Types
582  // -----------------------------------
583
584  /*
585  JdbcAppxB_6
586
587  getByte TINYINT
588          TINYINT, SMALLINT, INTEGER,
